sections.label: Episode 1
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Bass: a figure from countersubject 1, inverted (5 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted (3 times) and a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars.
sections.leads: From C minor to G minor

sections.label: Episode 2
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1 and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted and the opening of countersubject 1, in a sequence rising by a third every bar. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1. Bass: a figure from countersubject 1, in a sequence rising by a third every bar.
sections.leads: From G minor to C minor

sections.label: Episode 3
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times), in a sequence rising by a step every bar. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times) and the opening of countersubject 1, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Bass: free counterpoint, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Returns in Episode 4 (bars 80–94).
sections.leads: From C minor to F minor

sections.label: Episode 4
sections.summary: Reworks Episode 3 (bars 67–71), with soprano and alto exchanged, a fifth higher. Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times) and a figure from the subject and the opening of countersubject 1, in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Bass: a figure from the subject, inverted (3 times) and a figure from countersubject 1 and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every two bars.
sections.leads: From F minor to C minor

sections.label: Episode 5
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1 (7 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted (2 times) and the opening of countersubject 2 (2 times) and the opening of countersubject 1 and the opening of countersubject 2, inverted, in a sequence rising by a step every two bars. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 (4 times) and a figure from the subject (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 2, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Bass: a figure from countersubject 1 (9 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted (6 times) and a figure from the subject, in a sequence rising by a third every two bars.
sections.leads: Between two statements in C minor

sections.label: Episode 6
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1 (3 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times). Bass: a figure from countersubject 1.
sections.leads: From C minor to G minor

sections.label: Episode 7
sections.summary: Reworks the codetta (bars 18–22), with soprano and alto exchanged, at the same pitch level. Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted and the opening of countersubject 2. Alto: a figure from countersubject 2 (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1 and the opening of countersubject 2, in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Bass: a figure from countersubject 2 (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every two bars.
sections.leads: From G minor to C minor

sections.label: Coda
sections.leads: Perfect cadence in C minor at bar 185

spans.label: Codetta
spans.summary: Free counterpoint: nothing here is traced to the themes.

spans.label: Codetta
spans.summary: Soprano: a figure from countersubject 2 (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, in a sequence falling by a step every two bars. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted. Returns in Episode 7 (bars 161–168).
